findings.issue: The observed-share floor cancels TDM and contradicts M01. M07 floors the adjusted auto-driver share at 'the lowest same-basis CBD share loaded in M01' (candidate 33.1%). If that row is also the M01 baseline, which is the only destination row loaded, the floor equals the baseline and every TDM reduction becomes zero. The 33.1% is an all-purpose AM-period share for 'Vancouver CBD (Downtown, West End)'. It includes school, shopping and West End residents' trips, yet M07 applies it to commute trips only. It also sits above M01's own 'good ≤25%' office-commute line, so no scheme can reach 'good' through TDM.
findings.fix: Define the floor as a different, lower comparator: the best-performing same-purpose observed row, such as a measured downtown building or a later commute row, and require floor < baseline, otherwise disable the floor with a warning. Tag every share row with purpose (all purposes or commute) and refuse an all-purpose row as a commute floor. Make M01's 25% line and M07's floor use the same basis.

findings.issue: The spec names 'Census place-of-work' as the CBD-scale destination-end commute row and plans to 'identify the Census mode-by-place-of-work table'. The standard 2021 tables do not provide it. 98-10-0460-01 (residence-to-work flows by main mode) covers only CMAs and CAs. 98-10-0459-01 (CSD flows) is broken down by gender only. 98-10-0457/0458/0461-01 give mode by residence geography, and 98-10-0462-01 gives mode by commuting-destination category for residents. A downtown or CSD workplace-end mode share would need a paid custom tabulation, which is not deliverable by 7 Nov.
findings.fix: Record this as a FALSE ASSUMPTION. Drop Census from the 7 Nov critical path. Rely on the 2008 Vancouver-CBD row (S65), the 2011 Vancouver/UEL row (S66) and the 2023 dashboard destination-filter test. Keep a custom StatCan tabulation (2016 pre-COVID) as a post-competition item.

findings.issue: Every sourced mode row excludes the users that dominate hotel, cultural and kerb demand. S65 states 'Non-resident, commercial, and passenger-serving trips are not included'. Hotel guests and tourists are mostly non-residents, and drop-off and pick-up are passenger-serving. Yet M01 routes all 'attractions' to destination-end diary rows, and M05 sizes kerb bays from M01's taxi_TNC output, which has no source.
findings.fix: Add a third trip-end class, 'non-resident visitor', to M01 with its own SCENARIO badge. Block it from using diary rows (basis-mismatch badge). Add an explicit passenger-serving (drop-off/pick-up) and taxi/TNC share parameter feeding M05, labelled unsourced. List a hotel or visitor mode survey as a candidate source.

findings.issue: The fire-apparatus slot checks only a vehicle sweep. Building-code access-route geometry is a separate and usually governing test: route clear width, centreline radius, overhead clearance, gradient change, and the route's distance to the principal entrance and the FD connection (NBC/BCBC/VBBL Div B 3.2.5; reviewer recollection of about 6 m clear width, 12 m radius and 5 m overhead clearance, not verified this round). The default lane right-of-way is 6.1 m, legal width rather than clear width, so it is at or below such a width. Fire access may then be forced onto the arterial or the retail high street, which conflicts with M05's 'no curb cut on high street' and with M04 frontage use. No metric, parameter or sprint line covers this.
findings.fix: Add an 'access route' parameter set and metric with these fields: clear width, radius, overhead clearance, distance to principal entrance, distance to FD connection, and frontage used. Mark it unverified until a person transcribes VBBL or BCBC 3.2.5 (NBC 2020 is free from NRC). Add it to sprint item (d) and to the SYST hand-off.

verdict: FAIL. Round 3 fixed the occupancy arithmetic, the Trip Diary destination error, the status model and the tier-0 M03 scope. I confirmed the S65 Vancouver-CBD totals from the PDF. Entrants still cannot rely on the spec today. There are no checked by-law rows and no sourced employment density or trip rates, and owner names are still missing. Three new problems: M07's observed floor can cancel every TDM reduction and contradicts M01's 25% line. The Census place-of-work fallback does not exist as a standard table. Non-resident visitors and drop-off trips have no row. TCQSM ch.10 is freely downloadable, so M03's scale can be verified before 13 Nov. Fire access-route geometry is unmodelled. Web search was exhausted, so this round used direct fetches only.
